title: Hybrid Alignment via Constitutional Classifiers and Human Feedback for Jailbreak Resistance
summary: This paper proposes a hybrid alignment method combining constitutional classifiers (trained on synthetic data from natural language rules) with human feedback fine-tuning. The approach aims to defend against universal and many-shot jailbreaks while maintaining deployment viability through ablation studies isolating each component's contribution.
gap: While constitutional classifiers (ref-004) defend against universal jailbreaks, they fail against many-shot attacks (ref-038). Human feedback fine-tuning (ref-016) improves alignment but does not explicitly address jailbreak robustness. No prior work combines both to test if their hybrid mitigates both attack types.
approach: The method trains constitutional classifiers on synthetic data generated by LLMs using natural language rules (a 'constitution') to filter harmful outputs. These classifiers are integrated with human feedback fine-tuning (ref-016, ref-025) via a two-stage pipeline: (1) classifier filters outputs during supervised fine-tuning, (2) filtered outputs are ranked by human preferences. The hybrid differs from ref-004 by adding human feedback and from ref-016 by incorporating classifier-based filtering. Inputs: model outputs; outputs: filtered and preference-ranked responses; objective: minimize harmful content while preserving helpfulness.
evaluation: The method is evaluated on (1) ref-038's many-shot jailbreak dataset and (2) ref-014's automated jailbreak suffixes. Baselines include (a) constitutional classifiers alone (ref-004), (b) human feedback alone (ref-016), and (c) unaligned models. Metrics: (1) jailbreak success rate (binary: harmful content generated), (2) refusal rate (proportion of queries rejected), (3) inference overhead. Ablation studies compare hybrid vs. individual components on both attack types.
